parts.style: warm, gentle morning welcome, a soft smile
parts.text: Good morning. <short pause> Before the day starts asking things of you, take a moment here. <short pause> Today's devotional is called New Every Morning.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Perhaps you woke up rested. <short pause> Or perhaps you woke up already behind... with yesterday's argument still in your head, or a list that began before your feet touched the floor. <short pause> Either way, you are welcome here, just as you are.

Our verse comes from Lamentations, and that may seem a strange place to look for morning hope. <short pause> It is a book of grief. <short pause> Jerusalem had fallen. <short pause> Homes were in ruins, people were hungry, and so much of what they loved was gone.

The writer doesn't hide any of it. <short pause> He names his sorrow and his bitterness. <short pause> And then, in the middle of all that loss, he deliberately turns his mind toward something he knows to be true.
It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: His compassions fail not. <short pause> They are new every morning.
Notice what he does not say. <short pause> He doesn't say the trouble is gone by morning. <short pause> The city is still broken when the sun comes up. <short pause> What is new is the mercy.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Long before, when God's people crossed the wilderness, He fed them with manna. <short pause> They gathered enough for the day, and most days, they couldn't store it up for tomorrow. <short pause> They had to trust that when they woke, there would be bread again. <short pause> Mercy is a little like that. <short pause> You don't have this whole year's strength this morning. <short pause> You have today's.

So what did you carry over from yesterday? <short pause> A mistake you keep replaying? <short pause> A worry about someone you love? <short pause> A quiet feeling that you should be further along by now?

You can be honest about it, as the writer was. <short pause> And then you can set one true thing beside it. <short pause> God's compassion did not run out last night. <short pause> You are not starting today on what was left over. <short pause> You are starting on mercy that is new.

And mercy received can become mercy given. <short pause> Today, there may be someone who needs a fresh start from you. <short pause> A softer answer. <short pause> A second chance. <short pause> You could be the place where they find something new this morning.

Let's pray. <short pause> Faithful God, <short pause> thank You for waking me into mercy I did not earn. <short pause> I give You what I carried over from yesterday. <short pause> Give me strength enough for today, and make me gentle with the people I meet. <short pause> Great is Your faithfulness. <short pause> Amen.
As you go, carry these few words with you... <short pause> new every morning. <short pause> Say them at the door, at your desk, or in the middle of a hard hour. <short pause> Go gently into your day.
